items.title: Approximating solutions of fractional differential equations via a new faster iteration scheme in hyperbolic spaces
items.summary: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a new four-step fixed point iteration scheme in the framework of hyperbolic spaces as defined by Kohlenbach. We establish strong convergence theorems for the proposed iteration scheme for contractive-like mappings having a fixed point. Furthermore, we present a detailed rate analysis and prove that explicit error majorants for our iteration decay faster than those for the Abbas–Nazir iteration under suitable control-parameter assumptions. For positive affine contractions, this comparison also applies to actual errors. We also establish a data dependence result for the new scheme. Finally, we illustrate the theoretical findings through numerical examples…

items.summary: Background: Living systems can convert small physical or chemical perturbations into larger responses through selective molecular detection, signal transduction and nonlinear amplification. The 2026 Nobel Prizes in Physiology or Medicine, Physics and Chemistry provide distinct examples of optical control of excitable cells, inference from rare weakly interacting events and amplification of molecular asymmetry, respectively. These discoveries do not establish the efficacy or mechanism of biophoton therapy. Hypothesis: We propose a Weak-Signal Biological Amplification Hypothesis for neurological research. items.title: Wafer-scale integration of atomically thin metal oxide in memtransistor arrays for artificial neural networks
items.summary: Abstract Liquid metal printed (LMP) two-dimensional (2D) metal oxides offer unprecedented opportunities toward next-generation information storage and neuromorphic computing. However, the scalable manufacturing of LMP metal oxides based integrated electronic circuits for the complex neuromorphic applications remains challenging, due to low device yield and high device-to-device variability. Here we report the 2-inch wafer-scale synthesis of the ultrathin 2D stannous oxide (SnO) film with high crystallinity and uniformity by using the electrostatic-assisted LMP stripping technique at low temperature of 225 ℃. The integrated 32×32 vector-matrix SnO memtransistors in 48 independent blocks are…

items.title: Thermal stability of skyrmions.
items.summary: Magnetic skyrmions are vortex-like magnetic textures with a topologically nontrivial spin structure making a continuous transformation from the skyrmion to the uniform state impossible. Hence skyrmions are regarded as topologically protected attracting large interest concerning applications in data storage, neuromorphic computing, and digital logic. For such kind of applications an extraordinary stability of the skyrmion state against thermal fluctuations is required. In real matter, due to its discrete nature, topological protection translates into the existence of an energy barrier between the skyrmion and the uniform state leading to a finite skyrmion lifetime. Therefore the…

items.title: Ricci flow of Integrable Sigma Models, Hitchin Systems and Quantum Seiberg-Witten theory
items.summary: We construct a family of integrable 2d sigma models through 4d Chern-Simons theory and show that their classical point-particle reduction corresponds to a Hitchin system. The integrable Hitchin quantisation then provides a natural candidate Hamiltonian for the one-loop reduced dynamics of the sigma models, which coincides with the Perelman operator in all cases examined. This allows us to study the corresponding spectral problems using 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theory and 2d conformal field theory methods. For the sausage model, we derive exact quantisation conditions and compute exponentially small corrections essential for the agreement with numerical finite-volume results.

items.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
items.summary: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the…

items.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
items.summary: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing…

items.title: Volatility-Corrected Prediction Intervals: Locally Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: Prediction intervals from probabilistic time-series forecasters are commonly assessed by marginal coverage, the long-run proportion of observations falling inside the intervals. However, forecast errors in time series are often serially dependent and heteroskedastic, so prediction intervals can attain near-nominal marginal coverage while miscovering systematically during periods of larger local error variance. We identify and address this failure mode, which we call \emph{local scale miscalibration}. We first document the phenomenon using time-series foundation models (TSFMs): across several real-world series, their native intervals often attain near-nominal marginal coverage while…

items.title: Progress Probes $P^2$: Lightweight Runtime Monitoring for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform diverse manipulation tasks directly from visual observations and natural language instructions, but they remain prone to mistakes and unpredictable failures. Deploying these policies without continuous human supervision will require robust runtime monitors that detect when the policy has gone off-course. Existing monitors use external foundation models, such as vision-language models (VLMs) to supervise the policy, introducing significant complexity and computational cost for monitoring at runtime. In this work, we investigate an alternate approach: \textit{can a VLA's own internal activations provide the information needed to monitor its…

items.title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
items.summary: Institutions that deploy large language models in regulated settings often need technical evidence of responsible AI practices before approving a deployment. COMPL-AI provides a technical interpretation of the EU AI Act that organises this evidence under six principle groups and eighteen technical requirements, twelve of which current benchmarks can measure. The benchmark suites that produce this evidence are typically operated from a command line, while the staff who approve deployments are non-engineers. We present VERA, an open-source self-hosted dashboard deployed to facilitate responsible AI processes within a large European bank. A reviewer selects a model and runs public benchmarks…

items.title: From Quaternions to Pentarnions I: Algebra, geometry, and a spin model
items.summary: We introduce a family of five-dimensional non-flexible quadratic real algebras $\{\mathcal A_γ\}_{0\leqγ\leq1}$ with canonical basis $1,i,j,k,\ell$, in which $γ$ changes the multiplication but not their norm, and study how this change affects geometry and dynamics. The algebras are pairwise non-isomorphic, $\mathcal A_0$ contains Hamilton's quaternion algebra, and $\mathcal A_1$ is the Pentarnion algebra. The alternating part of the trilinear form $\langle u\times_γv,w\rangle$ induced by the multiplication of $\mathcal{A}_γ$ defines a three-dimensional subspace $H_γ\subset\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{i,j,k,\ell\}$, tilted by the angle $\arctan(γ/\sqrt3)$, whose rotation group…

items.title: A Fast Algorithm for Quaternion Tensor Singular Value Decomposition under the T-product
items.summary: Quaternion tensor singular value decomposition (T-SVD) under the T-product provides a framework for analyzing multidimensional quaternion data. However, the T-SVD construction of Pan and Ng (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl., 2024) \cite{PanNg2024} contains a structural gap: an unrestricted quaternion matrix SVD need not preserve the paired Fourier block structure required for tensor factor recovery, potentially leading to loss of T-unitarity and inaccurate reconstruction. To address this issue, we develop a structure-preserving construction that transforms each paired quaternion block into a complex matrix and maps its complex SVD factors back to quaternion factors with the required structure.…

items.title: MVLoMa: Multi-View Local Feature Matching with Any Geometry Foundation Model
items.summary: Local feature matching is typically formulated for image pairs, although structure-from-motion and visual localization commonly match one reference image against many retrieved or covisible neighbours. Applying a pairwise matcher independently to these centre-neighbour edges duplicates reference-side computation and prevents the matcher from exploiting complementary multi-view geometric evidence from the remaining observations. To address these limitations, we introduce MVLoMa, a sparse star-graph matcher that extends LoMa from image pairs to multiple views. MVLoMa first uses a frozen multi-view geometry model to jointly describe all images in a star, then injects the resulting cross-view…

items.title: Superintelligent Software Engineering: Governance That Scales with Capability
items.summary: Software agents are being trained to exceed human engineers; we argue that capability alone does not produce better software engineering. We define superintelligent software engineering as the discipline of building and evolving software with agents whose capability exceeds that of human engineers, in which governance (gates, contracts, decisions and decay control) scales with capability. The argument rests on three claims. First, correctness in a project rests on decisions and contracts that the code does not carry. Second, knowledge decays. Third, once an agent outpaces its reviewers, reading catches a shrinking share of the changes built on stale knowledge. A simple model shows that,…

items.title: Spark-Audio 1.0 Technical Report
items.summary: This paper introduces Spark-Audio 1.0, a speech foundation model trained on domestically produced computing infrastructure. The model accepts text and speech inputs and generates text outputs. It supports multilingual (99 languages) and multi-dialect (202 dialects) speech recognition, speech translation, audio perception and understanding, and both text- and speech-based dialogue, marking a shift from merely ``hearing clearly'' to genuinely ``understanding'' speech. Architecturally, Spark-Audio 1.0 couples a 0.65B-parameter dense audio encoder with a 30B-A3B Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model (LLM). The audio encoder is pretrained with representation-enhanced BEST-RQ and then…

items.title: DISC: Domain-Integrated Similarity Cost for Time-Series Dataset
items.summary: The growth of time-series datasets and foundation models has made dataset comparison a central part of time-series workflows. Assessing source-target transfer before model adaptation requires similarity estimates that can summarize transfer-related dataset relationships without exhaustive source-target evaluation over every candidate pair. Many metrics have been proposed for measuring similarity between time-series datasets, but they capture different dataset relationships and vary in how well they align with downstream utility across tasks. We evaluate this gap by measuring the correlation between source-target similarity scores and downstream forecasting errors in out-of-distribution and…

items.title: Learning Robot Behavior Priors from Non-Robotic Synthetic Data
items.summary: Real robot data, rich across tasks and morphologies, is often treated as the bottleneck for training robot learning models, including embodied foundation models that aim for zero-shot physical transfer. In this paper, we investigate the degree to which such models can acquire necessary structure using data from systems without embodiment. To this end, we test if inexpensive, procedurally generated synthetic data can yield useful priors before a model observes any real-world behavior. We study this through robot action prediction, a natural pretraining objective and a direct test of whether structure learned from arbitrary synthetic tasks transfers to embodied settings. We introduce three…

items.title: Trion-1: Unifying Language, Protein Sequence, and Structure with Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: We envision a general-purpose protein foundation model as a unified, interactive model of sequence, structure, and function, capable of understanding, generation, and cross-modal translation while retaining the instruction-following and reasoning capabilities of modern LLMs. Toward this vision, we introduce Trion-1, the first native, unified, multimodal diffusion language model (dLLM) for proteins. Trion-1 is built on two key design choices: (1) a unified discrete token space that jointly represents sequence, structure, and natural language; (2) a dLLM backbone that replaces strict left-to-right factorization with bidirectional or semi-bidirectional token interactions, enabling global…

items.title: Moving Regions, Not Moving Objects: Segmenting What Actually Moves under Camera Motion
items.summary: Moving object segmentation is conventionally formulated at the sequence and object level, marking an entire instance as moving once it moves anywhere in a video. Recent instantaneous formulations distinguish moving from stationary intervals, but still generate masks at the object level through frozen segmentation foundation models. Because the mask is derived from an instance-level proposal, motion is typically attributed to the entire instance rather than localized to the regions that actually move. Moreover, such instance-level predictions can produce masks even when no part of the instance is actually moving, revealing a more fundamental issue: motion is not an intrinsic property of an…

items.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
items.summary: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation…

items.title: Holographic surface defect RG flows without supersymmetry
items.summary: We consider $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory with gauge group SU$(N)$, which admits families of conformal surface defects defined by singular boundary conditions for scalar fields that completely break supersymmetry. At large $N$ and strong coupling, these defects are holographically dual either to a probe D5-brane or to one of two new D7-brane embeddings that we introduce in this work. We also construct embeddings of both D5- and D7-branes describing defect renormalisation group (RG) flows, for which the ultraviolet and infrared fixed points are both dual to the same D$p$-brane, with different values of a parameter. Our embeddings dual to RG flows are mostly constructed…

items.title: Track finding and particle identification performance with particle physics foundation models
items.summary: Modern high energy nuclear and particle physics experiments produce large amounts of sparse data that must be reduced significantly in size before performing physics analysis. Recently, there has been an effort to evaluate Foundation Models as a potential tool for performing data analysis. These models have been shown to learn features in high dimensional datasets based on the multi-modal data they are trained on. To show their effectiveness at performing complex pattern recognition tasks, such as reconstructing charged particles in a magnetic field, we evaluated the performance of a Foundation Model based reconstruction on several downstream tasks with a dataset composed of spacepoints in…

items.title: RGraph-Eval: Task-Grounded Scene Graphs for Evaluating Robot Video Generation
items.summary: Generated robot videos can look convincing while depicting the wrong interac- tion: a different object is moved, a grasp disappears, or a placement ends out- side its destination. We introduce RGraph-Eval, a reference-based framework that makes these discrepancies explicit through task-grounded temporal scene graphs. Unlike approaches that construct separate evidence representations for different evaluation dimensions, we organize task entities, interactions, and motion within a unified, interpretable scene graph representation. A foundation-model pipeline identifies manipulation roles, grounds persistent object masks, infers and verifies state transitions and action intervals, and…

items.title: nnInteractive Agent: General-Purpose AI Agents as 3D Image Annotators
items.summary: Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it. General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. We show that such agents can take over this work without additional training: the user makes a request in plain language, and the agent works out what has to be segmented, locates the targets, prompts nnInteractive, inspects the 3D result, corrects it and responds to feedback. Asked for 'the muscles used for chewing', an agent identifies and segments…

items.title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of In-Situ Soil Moisture and Temperature with a Time-Series Foundation Model
items.summary: Soil moisture and temperature govern plant-water availability and microbial activity, making them key indicators for evaluating land-restoration efforts on degraded landscapes. However, the physical and data-driven models normally used to forecast them both need information that a newly instrumented restoration site does not yet have: hydraulic parameters for the former and months of per-site training data for the latter. We evaluate TimesFM 1, a 500M-parameter time-series foundation model, zero-shot on 15-minute telemetry from 27 sensor stations across three land-management regimes (Control, Treatment, Scald) at a semi-arid restoration site, forecasting 5 cm and 30 cm soil moisture and…

items.title: Random Initialization as a Baseline for Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) use self-supervised pretraining to learn reusable representations for downstream tasks such as multivariate time series classification (MTSC). We examine how much pretrained weights contribute beyond the architecture itself by comparing seven publicly released instances from four TSFM families with architecture-matched randomly initialized counterparts on the UEA MTSC archive. For each instance, five random initializations are evaluated using four classifiers on frozen representations: ridge classification, logistic regression, RBF SVM, and random forest. After model-specific exclusions due to computational constraints, the study comprises 183 paired…

items.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
items.summary: We present IQuest-Q1, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic foundation model with 320B total parameters (15B activated). IQuest-Q1 is developed through a three-stage process: (1) stable and efficient pre-training, combining Stable SplitNorm, Muon, and muP with a two-stage curriculum whose second stage increases the coding-data mixture, preserving a wide stability margin between safe and optimal learning rates; (2) fine-grained mid-training, expanding the data mixture across domains and formats and progressively extending the context; and (3) multi-scaffold with multi-version post-training, combining SFT, domain-specialized RL, and MOPD across various scaffolds to integrate…

items.title: Same molecule, Different Knowledge: Cross-Identifier Binding Failures in LLMs For chemistry
items.summary: Chemical AI workflows routinely represent the same molecule through multiple co-referring identifiers, including trivial names, IUPAC names, and SMILES, implicitly assuming that these representations provide interchangeable access to an LLM's knowledge. To test this assumption, we first introduce a controlled benchmark and show that it does not hold. Across foundation models spanning 7B to 72B parameters, even chemistry-specialized models, co-referring molecular identifiers consistently expose different subsets of the model's knowledge. We then conduct a series of controlled behavioral, representational, and causal analyses to characterize this failure. We show that even when a model can…

items.title: CURTAIN: Towards a Foundation Model for Neutrino Telescopes
items.summary: Neutrino telescopes record more than a trillion photon detections per year, yet there does not exist a self-supervised learning (SSL) task which fully satisfies all three conditions: improving as the pretraining set grows, transferring to a different detector, and outperforming the best model trained without pretraining at all. We introduce CURTAIN, a temporal masking scheme and the first SSL task for neutrino telescopes that achieves all of these goals. Downstream performance monotonically improves with the number of pretraining events, as predicted by scaling laws. Our encoder builds on DeepIce, currently the leading model on the NuBench benchmarks direction reconstruction task.…

items.title: Synthetic-to-Real Code-Switched ASR: A Spontaneous Nepali-English Podcast Benchmark
items.summary: Nepali-English code-switched conversational speech presents severe challenges for automatic speech recognition (ASR), chiefly through script confusion (inappropriate mixing of Devanagari and Latin orthography) and elevated error rates at language switch points. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can adapt multilingual foundation models, but human code-switched audio is expensive to collect and annotate. We curate a new benchmark of 13,044 spontaneous podcast utterances (15.45 h total; 10,214 test, 2,830 dev), audited and verified to eliminate machine translation leakages and acoustic loops. We investigate a two-stage synthetic-to-real adaptation framework: Stage 1 applies SFT on 0.95 h of speech…

items.title: Quermassintegral inequalities for capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball
items.summary: In this paper, we study the quermassintegral inequalities for capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball in hyperbolic space. We construct a locally constrained nonlinear curvature flow that preserves the $k$-th quermassintegral while monotonically increasing the $l$-th quermassintegral for any $(1\leq l<k\leq n)$. Using this flow, we establish a full family of the quermassintegral inequalities for horo-convex capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball with contact angle $θ\in(0,π/2]$. Moreover, we weaken the horo-convexity to convexity and obtain the quermassintegral inequalities for convex capillary hypersurfaces between the $n$-th and $l$-th quermassintegrals.

items.title: Matter Induced Bounds: Photon Ring, Lyapunov Exponent, Induced Temperature
items.summary: We investigate analytic bounds on the equatorial photon ring radius and the Lyapunov exponent in rotating black holes containing anisotropic matter. For a constant equatorial equation-of-state parameter, the finite asymptotic mass and nonnegative energy density imply an upper bound on the photon ring radius given by the Kerr photon ring radius with the same asymptotic mass and rotation parameters for co-rotating and counter-rotating motions. The lower bounds are written in terms of the quantities evaluated at the outer horizon. These bounds on the Lyapunov exponent constrain the absolute magnitude of the imaginary part of the quasinormal frequency of a massless scalar field within the…

items.title: CVP-BAA: Efficiently Adapting Segment Anything Model for Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: Various task-specific medical segmentation models have demonstrated strong performance, their heavy reliance on extensive annotations and highly specialized architectures limits their versatility, scalability, and clinical applicability. Recently, adapting vision foundation models, particularly the segment anything model (SAM), has emerged as a promising alternative. However, prevalent parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, such as prompt tuning and adapter tuning, often lack an explicit mechanism to embed local structural priors into the long-range dependency modeling of vision transformers (ViT), rendering them insufficiently sensitive to fine-grained details. To address…

items.title: Know When to Escalate: Critic-Guided Adaptive Execution for Cloud-Local Embodied Agents
items.summary: Recent advances in foundation-model agents have enabled increasingly capable embodied systems for long-horizon planning and interaction. However, embodied agents require fast, closed-loop decisions as they continuously perceive and act on a changing environment. Deploying strong cloud agents leaves the platform idle for seconds between consecutive actions, while lightweight local models respond quickly but are more vulnerable to errors. Existing hierarchical architectures typically assign models fixed roles, whereas conventional model routers make stateless per-request decisions. We present CARE, a critic-guided adaptive execution framework that dynamically determines when to escalate…

items.title: Very tight embeddings of subspaces of \(L_p\) for \(0<p<1\)
items.summary: For \(0 1\), every \(d\)-dimensional subspace of \(L_p\) embeds linearly into \(\ell_p^{\lfloorμd\rfloor}\) with distortion at most \(C(p,μ)(\log(d+2))^{1/p}\). If its Rademacher type \(q\) constant is at most \(T\), where \(p<q\leq2\), the distortion is at most \(C(p,q,μ)T\), independently of \(d\). We also give explicit bounds as \(μ\downarrow1\). This answers the question of Johnson and Schechtman concerning the extension of their very tight embedding theorem below exponent one. The proof combines compression at a lower exponent with a change of density that preserves the number of coordinates, and applies over both scalar fields.

items.title: Biophoton emission from human palm during meditation: a multi‐method complexity analysis
items.summary: Biophotons are ultra-weak photon emissions in the visible spectrum produced by living organisms. While extensively studied in plants, germinating seeds, and cell cultures, in vivo measurements on the human body remain relatively rare, and no systematic multi-method complexity analysis of human ultraweak photon emission (UPE) under controlled physiological modulation has been reported to date. We address this gap by developing and applying a comprehensive analytical framework to UPE measurements from the right palm of a human subject. Three independent sessions were conducted on different days, each comprising four consecutive 15-min phases: a Dark reference, a pre-meditation resting state…

items.title: Non-Markovian Memory Kernels in Condensed-Phase Chemical Dynamics: From Dipole Dephasing and Conical Intersections to Spin Crossover and Radical-Pair Magnetoreception
items.summary: Standard theoretical formulations of ultrafast condensed-phase molecular processes rely heavily on Markovian master equations and time-local Lindblad semigroups that assume memoryless bath relaxation (t ≫ τB). However, in viscous solvents, structured protein binding pockets, and biomolecular matrices, environmental fluctuations exhibit power-law algebraic memory tails K(t) ∝ t−µ (µ ∈ (0, 1)) where Markovian approximations break down. In this work, we develop an analytical and computational framework for non-Markovian chemical dynamics governed by the causal Caputo fractional memory kernel of the Multi-Electron Unified Wave Equation (MEUWE). We apply this framework across five benchmark…

items.title: Inducing Tunable Volatile Analog Switching in Nanocomposite-Based MAPbBr3 Perovskite Memristors for Synaptic Emulation.
items.summary: Metal halide perovskites (MHPs) are promising candidates for memristive applications owing to their mixed ionic-electronic conductivity, yet their inherent instability and tendency toward abrupt resistive switching remain critical barriers to neuromorphic implementations. Here, we present a nanocomposite strategy in which MAPbBr3 nanocrystals are synthesized in situ within a nickel acetate matrix through a one-step, annealing-free, and glovebox-free process, enabling ambient-stable memristive devices. By modulating the perovskite volume fraction, the ionic-electronic dynamics are tuned, inducing a transition from abrupt, nonvolatile digital switching in polycrystalline MAPbBr3 to gradual,…

items.title: The Neutrino as an Open Helical Two-Photon State: Mass Scale, Helicity, and Tetrahedral Leading-Order Mixing
items.summary: Within Delta-c Mechanics the neutrino is proposed to be the same two-photon system as the electron, distinguished by orbital topology: the electron occupies a closed circular orbit, the neutrino an open helix. Its spin-½ representation is the pair spinor of the companion Clifford-algebra paper with mass parameter mν; the single-helicity limit is a boost along the spin axis, one chiral sector carrying the particle and the other suppressed as mν²/4E. Open (O7) are the identification of the open-orbit dynamics with that spinor and the Majorana condition, undecidable at the single-particle level; exchange statistics are inherited from the spin-statistics theorem. items.title: Spin-Clifford Bundles and Spin Connections on the Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
items.summary: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}^{H}=\mathcal{C}\ell(H_V)$, which is associated with hyperbolic space $H_V=V\oplus V^{*}$. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor…

items.title: Supercritical magnetic ray transforms in hyperbolic space: the complexification method from the transport-twistor lens
items.summary: We present new inversion formulas for the unattenuated and attenuated magnetic ray transforms in the Poincaré disk, in the case of a constant, supercritical magnetic field. Our approach mirrors earlier complexification approaches by Novikov (Ark. Mat., 2002) and Bal (J. Math. Pures Appl., 2005), and a second feature of this article is to connect the approach with the Transport Twistor framework recently introduced by Bohr-Paternain (J. Éc. polytech. items.title: TQFT gravity dual to the orbifold groupoid of Narain code CFTs over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
items.summary: In a companion paper arXiv:2610.26610, we classified the Narain conformal field theories obtained by gluing copies of the $A_3$ root and weight lattices along their $\mathbb{Z}_4$ discriminant group. For two hyperbolic pairs, this gives twenty-two even self-dual gluing codes, which fall into seven inequivalent theories at $c=\bar c=6$. In this paper, we develop the physical interpretation of this family and its connections to three-dimensional topological field theory. items.title: Recursive Self Improvement for Embodied Agents—A Survey of Mechanisms Evaluation and Open Challenges
items.summary: Embodied foundation models have expanded the range of instructions, observations, and actions that robots can process. Autonomy in execution, however, does not automatically provide autonomy in improvement. Robots must still diagnose failures, acquire useful experience, select interventions, and determine whether accepted changes improve future performance. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) connects these activities through persistent feedback and inheritance, with the stronger objective of improving the mechanisms that produce subsequent improvements. This survey distinguishes within-episode correction, persistent self-improvement, successive version inheritance, and meta-level…

items.summary: In Gamma Knife stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), achieving optimal dosimetric outcomes is physically constrained by complex tumor geometry. items.title: An Exact Clifford-Algebra Formalism for Quantum Gravity: A Controlled Four-Dimensional Covariant Action
items.summary: Quantum gravity requires a common language in which microscopic quantum structure, dynamical geometry, and the maps between them carry compatible mathematical types. We develop one from an eleven-generator real quadratic carrier of adopted signature (4,7), whose Clifford algebra Cl(4,7) has 2048 real basis blades; we call the resulting structure Rolandion algebra (R11). We establish an exact ordered-blade multiplication law, identify the 1024-dimensional even subalgebra, and separate 110 directed blade-replacement channels from the 55 metric-skew generators of so(4,7). items.title: Evolutionary Dynamics of Feral AI and the Emergence of Digital Ecosystems
items.summary: The digital world is approaching a profound phase transition, whose primary drivers, we argue, are different from those that dominate current discussions of AI risk. The transition need not begin with a superintelligent system escaping human control, or with an AI acquiring the ability and motivation to reproduce. Rather, we suggest that it may get under way as AI agents routinely delegate tasks by creating or recruiting other agents. As delegation becomes widespread and recursive, vast numbers of agents will be created; inevitably, some will persist, spread, and create others beyond their original tasks and environments. At scale, this changes the rules of the game. Digital environments…

items.title: Civilizational Unbinding Transition and the Demise of Human Warfare in the Superintelligence (SI) Society
items.summary: Abstract For millennia, large-scale inter-group violent conflict has been treated as an ineradicable structural feature of human civilization, with war mortality assumed to only follow a gradual, asymptotic downward trajectory. This study introduces the ‌Civilizational Unbinding Index (U)‌, a quantifiable framework that measures the progressive relaxation of natural, social and survival constraints across 10,000 years of human history, validated against the fully open Seshat Global History Databank. items.title: Dimensional convergence at the nanoscale: a novel synthesis of experimental evidence justifying direct measurement of quantum coherence in microtubules.
items.summary: We synthesize convergent experimental evidence from five independent research groups (2016-2025) addressing the longstanding "too warm, too wet" objection to quantum biology. items.title: Where the Loop Meets the Budget: Analyzing On-Device Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Language-model systems now rewrite their own memory, code, and weights, and small language models now run on phones and embedded boards. This paper asks whether the two developments have met: can a system improve itself within the memory, energy, thermal, latency, and connectivity budgets of a device? We define edge self-improvement as a verified update loop under a timevarying device budget, and we classify 63 works along three axes: the improved component, where computation ran in the reported evaluation, and the verification tier. Quantum Biology 2.0: Traversing and harnessing protein superhighway networks of light and life.
items.summary: As an emergent field stimulated by insights from the biological, chemical, physical, and quantum sciences, quantum biology explores how quantum phenomena such as superradiance, tunneling, and entanglement can be leveraged to enhance, influence, and probe biological processes across a diversity of scales and physical degrees of freedom. This review surveys key theoretical, computational, and experimental developments over the last decade, providing relevant historical background and scientific context going back as far as Bohr's 1932 lecture on "Light and Life" in Copenhagen. items.title: Hyperbolic Bipartite Network Model with Communities Impacts Sparse Neural Network Training
items.summary: Hyperbolic geometry explains many structural features of real-world networks, yet existing hyperbolic generative network models with community organization such as the nonuniform popularity-similarity optimization (nPSO) are restricted to unipartite graphs. Here we introduce a bipartite extension of the nPSO model called nBPSO, motivated by the prevalence of community organization in real-world bipartite networks and the emerging evidence of hyperbolic hierarchical connectivity in trained sparse neural networks. nBPSO provides explicit control over link density, degree distribution, average clustering, and community organization. items.title: Experimental platform to study the neuronal mechanisms of magnetoreception in the honey bee.
items.summary: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) offer an alternative model for investigating magnetoreception, exhibiting reliable navigation and behavioral responses to magnetic fields. Thanks to their compact brains, well-matched to the penetration depth of modern optical imaging techniques, they may offer insights into the neural and biochemical mechanisms underlying this sense, something that standard models, like migrating birds, have not so far provided. But also in honeybees, this progress requires tools capable of resolving weak, magnetically induced neural activity with high spatio-temporal precision. items.title: Toward quantum-informed addiction medicine: Coherence, entangled-photon imaging, and a theranostic hypothesis.
items.summary: Background Quantum biology has shown that selected biological processes depend on quantum effects, including coherence, tunnelling, and spin-dependent reactions. In parallel, quantum imaging now uses entangled photons to extract biological information at low photon flux. Early evidence that biological tissue can alter photon entanglement in disease-associated ways raises a translational question: whether decoherence itself can become a diagnostic signal.
